hyps.why: Replacing a removed direct input-to-output edge with a 3x3 conv restores a path and gains much more than replacing any other op.
Removing a 3x3 conv loses far more accuracy than removing a weaker op such as pooling or skip.
Reconnecting the last-hop edge into the output node with a conv gives a larger gain than swapping one op for another.
Filling an empty edge into the output with a conv gives a big gain compared with replacing existing ops.
Edge 0 feeds nodes 1 and 2 downstream, so restoring it with a conv gives a large gain.
Adding a conv where an edge was removed restores a useful path, giving more gain than replacing an existing op.
A skip replacing none restores gradient flow and gains, whereas skip replacing a conv typically loses accuracy.
Deleting a strong conv on the final edge costs more accuracy than deleting a weak op.
Removing a conv on the input edge that feeds the other nodes hurts more than removing a weak op.
Pooling in place of none adds a connection and gains, whereas pooling in place of a conv loses accuracy.
